again_cat: Back to Cat. Round the spine as you exhale.
again_chair: Chair again. Sit back, arms long.
again_chairtwist: Revolved Chair again. Twist from the ribs.
again_chaturanga: Shift forward and lower halfway down.
again_cow: And Cow. Drop the belly as you inhale.
again_cowface: Cow Face again. Clasp the hands behind the back.
again_crescentmoon: Crescent Moon again. Reach and lean.
again_deer: Back to Deer. Knees bent, sit tall.
again_dog: Back to Downward Dog. Hips high, heels heavy.
again_eagle: Eagle again. Wrap and sit low.
again_figurefour: Figure Four again. Ankle just above the knee.
again_forwardfold: Fold forward again. Let the head hang.
again_garland: Back to Garland. Low squat, chest lifted.
again_gate: Gate Pose again. Reach over the long leg.
again_halfmoon: Half Moon again. Open the top hip.
again_halfsplits: Half Splits again. Front leg long.
again_headtoknee: Head to Knee again. Fold over the straight leg.
again_highlunge: High Lunge again. Back heel lifted.
again_humblewarrior: Humble Warrior again. Fold inside the knee.
again_kneetonose: Knee to nose again. Round the back.
again_lizard: Back to Lizard. Hands inside the front foot.
again_lowlunge: Low Lunge again. Back knee down.
again_lungetwist: Lunge twist again. Open toward the front knee.
again_pigeon: Back to Pigeon. Square the hips.
again_plank: Back to Plank. One long line.
again_pyramid: Pyramid again. Fold over the front leg.
again_reclinedbigtoeside: Leg out to the side again.
again_reclinedpigeon: Reclined Figure Four again. Draw the leg in.
again_reversewarrior: Reverse Warrior. Top arm reaches back.
again_revtriangle: Revolved Triangle again. Open the chest.
again_savasana: Rest on your back again. Let the body grow heavy.
again_sideangle: Side Angle again. Top arm over the ear.
again_sidebend: Side bend again. Reach up and over.
again_sleepingpigeon: Sleeping Pigeon again. Fold forward and rest.
again_standingsplit: Standing Split again. Lift the back leg.
again_star: Back to Star. Arms and legs wide.
again_supinetwist: Twist again. Knees to the other side.
again_threadneedle: Thread the Needle again. Shoulder to the mat.
again_threeleggeddog: Three-Legged Dog again. Lift one leg high.
again_toestand: Toe Stand again. Balance on the balls of the feet.
again_triangle: Triangle again. Long through both sides.
again_updog: Upward Dog. Lift the chest, roll the shoulders back.
again_warrior1: Warrior One again. Hips face forward.
again_warrior2: Back to Warrior Two. Open the arms.
again_warrior3: Warrior Three again. One long line.
again_widefoldtwist: Twist in the wide fold again.
bigtoe: Hand to Big Toe. Stand tall and draw one knee up. Hold the big toe or the shin, then extend the lifted leg forward toward hip height. Keep the standing leg straight, and straighten the lifted leg as far as you can. Stay tall, and if you lean, lean from the hips, not by rounding the back. Breathe smoothly. A strap around the foot helps, or keep the knee bent.
bigtoeside: Hand to Big Toe, side. Stand tall and lift one knee. Hold the big toe, or loop a strap around the foot. Straighten the lifted leg and open it to the side. Keep the standing leg straight. Stay tall, not leaning toward the lifted leg. For an easier option, keep the knee bent. Breathe.
birddog: Bird Dog. Start on your hands and knees. Reach one arm straight forward at shoulder height and the opposite leg straight back at hip height. Keep your back flat and do not arch to lift higher. Keep your hips level and square to the floor. Breathe steadily and stay long.
birdofparadise: Bird of Paradise. From Bound Side Angle, step the back foot forward and stand up slowly, keeping the hands clasped around the thigh. Straighten the standing leg. Then extend the bound leg straight out and up. Stand tall and avoid leaning away from the bound leg. Breathe slowly. Keep the lifted knee bent if needed.
boat: Boat. Sit with the knees bent and the feet flat. Lean back with a long spine, and lift the feet. Keep the chest lifted so the back does not round. Bring the shins level, or straighten the legs if you can. Reach the arms forward, parallel to the floor. Breathe steadily. For an easier version, keep the toes down.
boundangle: Bound Angle. Sit tall and bring the soles of the feet together, letting the knees open out to the sides. Hold the ankles or feet. Stack the shoulders over the hips and keep both shoulders level. Let the knees release toward the floor without pressing them down. If the knees are high or the back rounds, sit on a folded blanket or move the feet further away. Stay here and breathe slowly. Lengthen the spine as you breathe in. Soften the hips and thighs as you breathe out.
boundsideangle: Bound Side Angle. From Side Angle, bend the front knee over the ankle and keep the back leg straight. Thread the bottom arm under the front thigh, reach the top arm behind you, and clasp the hands or hold a strap. Lengthen the torso over the front thigh, then roll the chest open toward the ceiling. Breathe evenly. If the bind is tight, keep the bottom hand on a block.
bow: Bow. Lie on your belly, bend the knees, and draw the heels toward your seat. Reach back and hold the outer ankles. Breathing in, kick the feet into the hands to lift the chest. Let the thighs lift off the mat. Breathe into the chest. To ease it, hold a strap around the ankles.
bridge: Bridge. Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, parallel and hip-width apart. Walk the heels close enough that the fingertips can almost touch them. Press into the feet and lift the hips. Keep the knees stacked over the ankles, not falling in or out. Keep the neck still. Breathe steadily. A block under the sacrum gives you an easier, supported version.
camel: Camel. Kneel with the knees hip-width apart and rest the shins and the tops of the feet on the mat. Press the hips forward over the knees, lift through the chest, and lean back. Reach the hands toward the heels, or rest them on blocks. Breathe slowly. If the lower back pinches, hold the lower back instead.
cat: Cat. From hands and knees, keep the wrists under the shoulders. Breathe out and round the upper back toward the ceiling, tucking the chin toward the chest.
chair: Chair. Stand with the feet hip-width apart. Bend the knees and sit the hips back as if lowering onto a chair. Keep your weight in the heels so the knees stay over or behind the toes. Hinge slightly from the hips, with the chest lifted and the back long. Reach the arms up alongside the ears, elbows straight, fingertips reaching up. Breathe steadily. If the thighs tire, rise a little and keep the shape.
chairtwist: Revolved Chair. From Chair, press the palms together at the chest. Sit deeper, then twist and hook the elbow outside the opposite knee. Keep both knees even, so neither slides forward in the twist. Keep the weight in the heels and lift the chest as you turn. Breathe in to lengthen the spine, breathe out to rotate. To make it easier, keep the hands at the chest without hooking the elbow.
chaturanga: Four-Limbed Staff. From plank, lower until the elbows reach ninety degrees, hugged in over the wrists. Shoulders stay level with the elbows. Breathe out. Knees down is fine.
child: Child's Pose. Kneel with the big toes touching and the tops of the feet resting on the mat. Sink the hips back toward the heels and fold the torso forward over the thighs. Rest the forehead down. Walk the hands forward along the mat, or rest the arms by your sides, whichever feels better. If the hips do not reach the heels, place a folded blanket between them. Breathe slowly into the back of the ribs and let each exhale be a little longer.

clip_welcome: Welcome. Set up your mat where you can see the screen. We start standing at the top of the mat. Take a slow breath in, and a long breath out.
cobra: Cobra. Lie on your belly, hands under the shoulders, tops of the feet pressing down. Lift the chest using the back muscles, not the arms. Keep a soft bend in the elbows and hug them in by the ribs. Lift only as high as your back allows. Breathe in as you rise.
compass: Compass. Sit with one knee bent and lift that leg over the shoulder. Hold the outside of the foot with the opposite hand. Press the supporting hand down by the hip. Straighten the lifted leg behind the shoulder and turn the chest away from it. Breathe steadily. Keep the knee bent if needed.
cow: Cow. From hands and knees, let the belly sink toward the mat. Lift the chest and the tailbone. Keep the wrists under the shoulders. Gaze slightly forward and breathe in fully.
cowface: Cow Face. Sit tall and reach your top arm up, then bend the elbow and drop that hand between your shoulder blades. Bring the bottom arm behind you and slide the back of that hand up your spine. Point the top elbow to the ceiling and the bottom elbow to the floor. Clasp your hands behind your back, or hold a strap between them. Do not let the top arm pull your chest or head forward. Keep sitting tall. Breathe into the side ribs and the back of the chest.
cradle: Baby Cradle. Sit with the legs crossed. Lift one shin and hold it in the crooks of the elbows, foot in one elbow and knee in the other. Hold the shin parallel to the floor. Sit tall and hug the shin toward the chest. Rock gently from side to side if it feels good. Keep the shoulders relaxed. Breathe slowly. If this is hard to hold, keep the shin lower and hold the foot and knee with the hands.
crane: Crane. Squat with the hands down and the knees high on the upper arms. Lean forward and lift the feet. Press the floor away and straighten the arms. Lift the hips higher than the shoulders. Breathe evenly. Keep the elbows bent if you need to.
crescentmoon: Crescent Moon. Stand tall with the feet together and reach both arms up alongside the ears. Press the palms together. Breathing out, lean to one side, bending from the waist. Keep both legs straight and the hips level. Keep the chest open, not folding forward. Breathe into the long side of the body.
crow: Crow. Squat, hands flat, fingers spread forward. Bend the elbows into a shelf and rest the knees high on the upper arms. Shift the shoulders forward past the wrists until the feet lift. Breathe evenly. Lift one foot at a time if you need.
cue_arms_down: Release your arms down by your sides.
cue_back_knee_down: Lower the back knee gently to the mat.
cue_back_knee_up: Tuck the back toes, and lift the back knee.
cue_back_to_child: Sink your hips back toward your heels.
cue_come_down: Lower your legs slowly, and rest.
cue_feet_down: Slowly bring your feet back down to the mat.
cue_feet_in: Bend your knees, and plant your feet close to your hips.
cue_fold_forward: Breathe out, hinge at the hips, and fold forward.
cue_fold_from_squat: Lift your hips, and fold over your legs.
cue_foot_down: Lower your lifted foot back to the mat.
cue_hands_down: Plant your hands on the mat, shoulder-width apart.
cue_hands_frame: Bring your hands down to frame the front foot.
cue_hands_heart: Bring your palms together at your heart.
cue_headstand_setup: Interlace your fingers, and place the crown of your head on the mat between your forearms.
cue_hips_up: Lift your hips up and back.
cue_knees_down: Drop your knees gently to the mat.
cue_legs_over: Lift your legs, and roll your hips up and over.
cue_lie_back: Lower down onto your back, one vertebra at a time.
cue_lift_chest_arms: Lift your chest, and sweep your arms up.
cue_lift_left: Shift your weight onto your right foot, and lift your left foot.
cue_lift_right: Shift your weight onto your left foot, and lift your right foot.
cue_lower_down: Lower slowly, all the way down to the mat.
cue_lower_hips: Lower your hips gently back to the mat.
cue_lunge_to_pigeon: Lower the front knee behind your wrist, and slide the back leg long.
cue_pigeon_to_dog: Tuck the back toes, and press back to Down Dog.
cue_pigeon_to_lunge: Tuck the back toes, and lift into a lunge.
cue_press_back: Tuck your toes, and press your hips back and up.
cue_press_up: Tuck your toes, and press back up.
cue_rise_from_lunge: Step the back foot forward, and rise to standing.
cue_rise_knees: Lift your chest, and come up onto your knees.
cue_rise_squat: Plant your feet, and rise into a squat.
cue_rise_stance: Spin the back heel down, and rise up.
cue_rise_up: Soften the knees, and roll up slowly to standing, head last.
cue_roll_down: Slowly roll your spine back down, one vertebra at a time.
cue_shift_forward: Shift your shoulders forward over your wrists, into plank.
cue_sit_back: Bend your knees, and sit your hips back.
cue_sit_down: Lower your seat gently down to the mat.
cue_sit_up: Roll onto one side, and press yourself up to sitting.
cue_squat_down: Bend your knees and sink down into a squat.
cue_stand_from_knees: Step one foot forward, and press up to standing.
cue_step_back: Step your feet back, one at a time.
cue_step_back_dog: Step the front foot back, into Down Dog.
cue_step_back_left: Plant your hands, and step your left foot back into a lunge.
cue_step_back_long_left: Take a big step back with your left foot.
cue_step_back_long_right: Take a big step back with your right foot.
cue_step_back_plank: Plant your hands, and step or hop back to plank.
cue_step_back_right: Plant your hands, and step your right foot back into a lunge.
cue_step_back_to_plank: Step the front foot back, into plank.
cue_step_forward_left: Step your left foot forward, between your hands.
cue_step_forward_right: Step your right foot forward, between your hands.
cue_step_to_front: Step the back foot forward, to meet the front.
cue_straighten: Straighten your legs, and stand tall.
cue_swing_sit: Swing your legs around, and come to sit.
cue_to_tabletop: Come onto your hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
cue_tripod_setup: Place your hands flat, shoulder-width apart, and set the crown of your head in front of them.
cue_tuck_lift: Tuck your toes, and lift your hips high.
cue_turn_front: Turn to face the front of your mat.
cue_turn_side: Turn to face the long side of your mat.
cue_walk_to_hands: Walk or hop your feet up to your hands.
dancer: Dancer. Stand on one leg and hold the inside of the lifted foot with the same-side hand. Keep the standing leg straight, hip over the ankle. Kick the lifted foot back into the hand as the chest tips forward, and reach the front arm forward and up. Tip forward only as far as you stay balanced. Breathe slowly. Hold a wall if you need.
deer: Deer. Sit with one leg bent in front and the other bent behind you, both knees at about ninety degrees. Let the knees rest toward the floor. Sit tall, and let the hips settle unevenly if they need to. You can stay here, or fold forward over the front shin and rest on the forearms. If the hips feel uncomfortable, sit on a cushion. Keep the shoulders soft. Breathe slowly and stay still. If you feel a pinch in either knee, ease out a little.
dog: Downward Dog. From hands and knees, tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back into an upside down V. Point the fingers to the top of the mat. Straighten the elbows and press through the palms. Open the shoulders and let the chest move toward the thighs. Keep the feet parallel and let the heels sink toward the mat. They do not need to touch. Bend the knees as much as you need to keep the back long. Breathe slowly and let the backs of the legs lengthen.
dolphin: Dolphin. From hands and knees, lower onto the forearms with the elbows under the shoulders. Tuck the toes and press the hips up and back. Walk the feet in a little, keeping the shoulders stacked close above the elbows. Straighten the legs as far as the hamstrings allow, and keep the knees bent if the back starts to round. Press the forearms down. Breathe steadily, and let the head hang between the arms.
eagle: Eagle. Bend the knees and cross one thigh over the other. Sit lower into the standing leg. Cross the arms at the elbows, wrap the forearms, and lift the elbows to shoulder height. Keep the hips square and level, and lift the chest so the torso stays upright. Breathe steadily. The top toes can touch the floor for balance.
earpressure: Ear Pressure. Lie on your back and roll the legs up and over into plow. Bend the knees and lower them beside the ears. Keep the hips lifted over the shoulders. Keep the neck still and do not turn the head. Breathe softly into the back of the body. To make it easier, place a folded blanket under the shoulders.
easy: Easy Pose. Sit on your mat and cross your shins, each foot resting under the opposite knee. Sit tall through the crown of your head. If your lower back rounds, raise your hips on a cushion or folded blanket. Level your shoulders and let them relax away from your ears. Let your knees drop toward the floor without forcing them. Rest your hands on your thighs. Breathe in through the nose and let the breath fill the ribs, then breathe out slowly. Stay steady and keep the spine long.
eightangle: Eight Angle Pose. Hook one leg over the shoulder and cross the ankles. Bend the elbows toward ninety degrees. Extend the legs to the side, squeezing the arm. Keep the chest low. Breathe.
fallentriangle: Fallen Triangle. From plank, shift onto your supporting hand and thread one leg under you, out to the side. Straighten the supporting arm and the threaded leg. Lift your hips and open your chest. Breathe.
figurefour: Standing Figure Four. Stand tall, then cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, just above the standing knee. Flex the lifted foot to protect the knee. Bend the standing leg and sit back as if into a chair. Keep the chest lifted and the spine long as you hinge from the hips. Breathe steadily. To make it easier, keep a hand on a wall.
firefly: Firefly. Squat, slide the shoulders behind the knees, and plant the hands. Straighten the arms. Lean back and lift the feet, extending the legs forward and level with the hips. Breathe. Keep the knees bent to practice.
firelog: Fire Log. Sit tall with your knees bent. Rest your bottom shin on the mat parallel to the front edge, then stack the top shin over it, ankle over knee, like logs. Flex both feet to protect your knees. If the top knee floats high, slide a block or blanket under it. Sit tall first. Lean forward only if you can keep the spine long, folding from the hips. Rest your hands on the floor in front of you. Breathe slowly into the outer hips.
fish: Fish. Lie on your back with legs long. Slide your hands under your hips and press into your forearms to lift your chest. Rest the crown of your head lightly on the mat with little weight on it. Keep your legs straight and active. For an easier option, rest your upper back on a block. Breathe into your chest.
flyingpigeon: Flying Pigeon. From Standing Figure Four, fold and hook the lifted foot around the upper arm. Bend the elbows into a shelf. Shift forward until the back foot floats, then extend the back leg straight behind you. Breathe.
flyingsplits: Flying Splits. Bend the elbows to ninety degrees and rest the front thigh on the arm. Shift the chest past the wrists. Extend the front leg forward and lift the back leg. Breathe steadily.
forearmplank: Forearm Plank. From hands and knees, lower onto the forearms with the elbows under the shoulders. Press the forearms flat into the mat. Step the feet back and come onto the balls of the feet. Lift the hips into one line from shoulders to heels, without piking up or sagging. Press back through the heels. Breathe steadily. For an easier version, lower the knees and keep the same long line
forearmstand: Forearm Stand. Press the forearms flat and parallel, shoulders over the elbows. Walk the feet in and lift one leg, then the other. Stack the hips over the shoulders and reach the feet straight up. Breathe steadily. Practice with the heels near a wall.
forwardfold: Standing Forward Fold. From standing, breathe out and fold forward from the hips, leading with the chest. Bend the knees as much as you need to bring the belly toward the thighs. Keep the hips stacked over the ankles and the heels on the mat, with your weight toward the balls of the feet. Straighten the legs only as far as is comfortable while the back stays long. Let the head and neck relax. Rest the hands on the shins or blocks. Breathe slowly.
frog: Frog. Come to hands and knees, then walk the knees wide apart. Keep each shin at ninety degrees to the thigh, ankles in line with the knees. Lower onto the forearms and let the hips ease back. Keep the spine long and the neck relaxed. Pad the knees with a blanket, and rest the forehead on the hands or a block. Breathe slowly into the belly and inner thighs. If the stretch is too strong, bring the knees closer or shift the hips back. Stay still.
frogbackbend: Half Frog. Lie on your belly, propped on one forearm. Bend the other knee and take the top of that foot with the hand. Press the foot down beside the hip. Press into the forearm and lift the chest. Keep the other leg straight along the mat. Breathe slowly. Ease off if the knee strains.
garland: Garland. Stand with the feet a little wider than the hips, toes turned out. Bend the knees and sink the hips down toward the heels into a deep squat. Bring the palms together at the heart and press the elbows into the inner knees. Lift the chest and lengthen through the crown. Let both heels ground. If they lift, place a rolled mat or a folded blanket under them. Breathe slowly, and let each exhale settle the hips a little lower.
gate: Gate. Kneel tall, then extend one leg out to the side with the sole on the mat. Keep the extended leg straight and stack your hip over the kneeling knee. Rest your bottom hand on the extended leg. Reach the top arm up and over as you lean toward the straight leg. Keep the chest open. Breathe into the long side of your ribs.
goddess: Goddess. Step the feet wide and turn the toes out, about forty-five degrees. Bend the knees and sink the hips toward knee height. Press the knees out so they track over the toes, and keep each knee stacked over its ankle. Stack the shoulders over the hips rather than leaning forward, and sink evenly so the hips stay level. Rest the hands at the heart or on the thighs. Breathe slowly and stay steady.
gorilla: Gorilla. Stand with the feet hip width apart, bend the knees, and fold forward from the hips. Slide the palms under the soles of the feet, toes reaching to the wrists. Straighten the legs as far as comfortable, and keep the knees soft if the back starts to round. Fold deeper with each exhale and let the head hang. Breathe slowly. If the hands do not reach, hold the shins or the backs of the ankles instead.
halfboat: Half Boat. Sit with your knees bent and feet on the floor. Lean back a little and lift your feet so your shins are parallel to the floor. Lift your chest and keep the back long, not rounded. Reach your arms forward alongside your knees. For an easier option, hold the backs of your thighs. Breathe steadily.
halfbow: Half Bow. Lie on your belly on one forearm. Bend the other knee, hold the ankle with the free hand. Kick the foot into the hand to lift the chest. Keep the other leg long. Breathe steadily. Use a strap if needed.
halfhero: Half Hero Fold. Sit with one leg long in front of you. Fold the other leg back so the foot rests beside the hip, toes pointing back. Keep the extended leg straight and the foot flexed. Sit tall, then hinge from the hips. Fold evenly over the straight leg, leading with the chest. Breathe in to lengthen, out to fold. If the folded knee strains, sit on a blanket.
halflift: Halfway Lift. Rest the fingertips on the shins and lift the chest until the back is flat. Soften the knees if you need. Breathe in as you lift.
halflotus: Half Lotus. Sit on the mat and fold one leg in. Place the top foot high on the opposite thigh, close to the hip crease. Let the bottom knee rest on the floor. If the knees sit higher than the hips, sit on a folded blanket. Sit tall through the crown of the head. Rest the hands on the knees and keep the shoulders soft. Breathe slowly in and out through the nose. If you feel any pain in the knee, take the foot down and sit cross-legged instead.
halfmoon: Half Moon. From Triangle, bend the front knee and place the bottom hand on the floor under the shoulder. Straighten the standing leg as the top leg lifts to hip height. Flex the lifted foot, toes pointing the same way as your chest. Stack the top arm over the bottom arm and reach up through the fingertips. Breathe evenly. A block under the hand helps.
halfsplits: Half Splits. From a low lunge with the back knee down, shift the hips back until they are stacked over the back knee. Straighten the front leg, heel down and toes up. Flex the front foot, drawing the toes toward you. Hands on the floor or on blocks. Breathing in, lengthen the spine. Breathing out, fold forward over the front leg, leading with the chest. Keep the back long rather than rounded. If the hamstrings are tight, keep a bend in the front knee. Breathe slowly.
handstand: Handstand. Plant the hands shoulder width apart, and kick or float the legs up. Straighten the arms and push the floor away. Stack the hips over the shoulders and the feet over the hips. Keep the legs together and toes pointed. Breathe. Practice against a wall.
handunderfoot: Hands Under Feet. Stand with your feet hip width apart. Fold forward from the hips, bending your knees as much as you need. Slide your palms under your feet, toes toward the wrist creases. Bring your chest toward your thighs, keeping the spine long. Straighten the legs only as the hamstrings allow. Let your head hang and your neck relax. Breathe slowly.
happybaby: Happy Baby. Lie on your back and draw your knees toward your chest. Hold the outer edges of your feet, your ankles, or the backs of your thighs. Open your knees wider than your torso and draw them toward your armpits. Stack your ankles over your knees, soles toward the ceiling. Keep your lower back and head resting on the mat. If the tailbone lifts, ease the pull with the hands. Rock gently side to side if it feels good. Breathe slowly into the hips and lower back.
headstand: Supported Headstand. Kneel, set the forearms on the mat, and clasp the hands. Place the crown of the head down, cupped by the hands. Press the forearms down and lift the shoulders, so the neck carries little weight. Walk the feet in until the hips are stacked over the shoulders. Lift the legs and reach the feet straight up over the hips. Breathe slowly. Practice near a wall, or stay with the knees bent.
headstandsplit: Straddle Headstand. Come into headstand with the forearms firmly grounded. Stack the hips over the shoulders. Open the legs wide, both at the same height. Straighten both legs and reach out through the feet. Press the forearms down so the neck stays light. Breathe slowly. Practice near a wall if you need support, and come down with control.
headtoknee: Head to Knee. Sit with one leg extended and bend the other knee, resting that sole against the inner thigh of the straight leg. Keep the extended leg straight and flex the foot, toes toward you. Inhale and lengthen your spine. Exhale and fold forward from the hips over the straight leg. Keep the back long rather than rounding to reach. If the hamstrings are tight, bend the knee slightly or loop a strap around the foot. Breathe slowly and soften a little more on each exhale.
hero: Hero. Kneel with your knees together and your feet a little wider than your hips, tops of the feet on the mat. Sit down between your heels. If your hips do not reach the floor, sit on a block. Keep your knees close together and lengthen up through your spine. Rest your hands on your thighs, palms down. Let your shoulders soften away from your ears. If you feel any strain in the knees, sit higher. Breathe steadily through the nose and let each inhale lift you a little taller.
heron: Heron. Sit with one leg folded back beside the hip and the other knee bent in front. Hold that foot with both hands. Straighten the lifted leg toward the ceiling. Sit tall and draw the leg toward you rather than rounding to it. Breathe slowly. Use a strap, or keep the knee bent, if the back rounds.
highlunge: High Lunge. Step one foot back a long stride and stay on the ball of the back foot, heel lifted over the toes. Bend the front knee toward ninety degrees, knee stacked over the ankle. Press back through the back heel to keep the back leg straight. Lift the torso upright over the hips and reach the arms up alongside the ears, fingertips toward the ceiling. Breathe steadily and keep the hips level.
humblewarrior: Humble Warrior. From a lunge with the back heel down, clasp the hands behind you. Bend the front knee deeply and keep the back leg straight. Breathing out, fold the torso down inside the front leg, letting the shoulder move toward the inner knee. Lift the clasped hands away from the back. Breathe slowly. If the bind is tight, hold a strap between the hands.
intro_ashtanga: we'll be doing an Ashtanga practice, following the primary series. We'll start with sun salutations, move through standing and seated poses with five breaths in each, and finish with the closing sequence.
intro_backbends: we'll be exploring backbends. We'll warm up the spine gently first, then open the front of the body step by step. Keep the breath easy.
intro_balance: we'll be working on balance. Standing on one leg, finding a steady gaze, and staying calm when we wobble. Wobbling is part of it.
intro_balanced: we'll be doing an all-round practice, a little of everything. We'll warm up, build some strength and balance, open the body, and finish with a rest.
intro_evening: we'll be doing a wind-down practice. Slow, quiet poses, long breaths out, and a long rest at the end. Let the day go.
intro_flexibility: we'll be working on flexibility. Slow, steady stretches for the hamstrings, the hips and the spine. Never force a stretch; let the breath do the work.
intro_general: we'll be doing a practice put together just for you. Follow the screen and my voice, and rest whenever you need to.
intro_hips: we'll be opening the hips. We'll take our time with lunges, folds and longer floor poses, and let the body soften a little more with every breath out.
intro_morning: we'll be doing a wake-up practice. Gentle movement, a few energising poses, and plenty of breath to get the body going.
intro_strength: we'll be doing a strength practice. We'll work the legs, the core and the arms, and hold some poses a little longer. Go at your own pace.
intro_vinyasa: we'll be doing a vinyasa flow. We'll move with the breath, one breath for each movement, linking the poses together like a dance.
intro_yin: we'll be doing a yin practice. We'll stay in each pose for a few minutes, relax the muscles, and let gravity do the work. It's quiet, but not always easy.
kingdancer: King Dancer. Stand on one leg and bend the other knee behind you. Reach both arms overhead and catch the lifted foot. Straighten the standing leg. Lift the chest and arch from the upper back. Breathe steadily. Use a strap around the foot to make it easier.
kingpigeon: King Pigeon. From pigeon, bend the back knee and reach both arms overhead to hold the back foot. Keep the hips square to the front. Lift the chest and arch from the upper back. Breathe slowly. Use a strap if you cannot reach.
kneeplank: Knee Plank. From your hands and knees, walk your hands forward and lower your hips. Stack your shoulders over your wrists. Make one line from shoulders to hips to knees. Draw your belly in gently and keep your neck long. Press the floor away through your hands. Breathe steadily.
kneeschaturanga: Knees Down Chaturanga. From knee plank, lower until your elbows bend to a right angle. Elbows tuck back along the ribs. Hips stay in line. Exhale.
kneeschestchin: Knees, Chest, Chin. From plank, lower the knees, chest and chin. Keep the hips lifted and the elbows tucked by the ribs. Breathe out as you lower.
kneesideplank: Side Plank with Knee Down. From hands and knees, keep the bottom knee down and extend the top leg long, foot flat on the mat. Stack the supporting shoulder over the wrist and straighten the supporting arm. Lift the hips and reach the top arm straight up. Breathe evenly and keep the body in one long line.
kneestochest: Knees to Chest. Lie on your back and draw both knees in toward your chest. Wrap your arms around your shins, or hold the backs of your thighs. Hug your knees in gently. Keep your whole back resting on the mat, including your head and shoulders. Let your tailbone stay heavy rather than curling off the floor. Relax your shoulders away from your ears. Breathe into your belly against your thighs, and let each exhale soften the lower back.
kneetonose: Knee to Nose. From downward dog, shift into plank and draw one knee toward your nose. Round your upper back. Press the floor away through straight arms. Exhale.
koundinya1: Koundinya One. From side crow, bend the elbows to make a shelf. Scissor the legs apart, top leg back, bottom leg forward. Straighten both legs fully. Keep breathing. Bend a knee if needed.
legraises: Leg Raises. Lie on your back with the legs straight up and the hands under the hips or by your sides. Lower the legs to about forty-five degrees. Keep both legs straight. Keep the lower back pressing into the mat. Breathe steadily. If the back arches, lift the legs higher or bend the knees.
legsup: Legs Up the Wall. Sit sideways next to the wall, then swing your legs up as you lie back. Move your hips close to the wall so your legs rest straight up against it. Let both legs stay straight but soft, with the backs of the legs supported by the wall. If your hamstrings feel tight, move your hips back a little. Rest your arms by your sides, palms up. Breathe slowly and evenly, and let the exhale be a little longer than the inhale. Stay here and rest.
lion: Lion. Kneel and sit back on the heels. Press the palms onto the knees, fingers spread. Lean the chest slightly forward with a long spine. Breathe in through the nose. Breathe out through the mouth, tongue out, eyes up. Repeat a few times.
lizard: Lizard. From a lunge, step the front foot toward the outside edge of the mat, so the knee is outside the shoulder. Keep the front knee bent over the ankle. Lengthen the back leg, or lower the back knee for an easier version. Walk the hands inside the front foot and lower the chest toward the floor. Come down to the forearms or rest them on blocks. Keep the spine long. Breathe slowly into the hips, and soften a little more with each exhale.
locust: Locust. Lie on your belly with the arms alongside the body, palms down. Breathing in, lift the chest using the muscles of the back. Lift the legs off the mat and keep them straight, reaching through the toes. Reach the arms back toward the feet. Keep the neck long. Breathe steadily.
lotus: Lotus. Sit with your legs crossed, then lift one foot onto the opposite thigh, and the second foot onto the other thigh. Move slowly and only as far as your hips allow. Let your knees release toward the floor. If a knee lifts or you feel any pull in the knee, come into half lotus with one foot on the floor instead. Sit tall through the crown and level your shoulders. Rest your hands on your knees. Breathe evenly through the nose.
lowlunge: Low Lunge. From a lunge, lower the back knee and rest the top of the back foot on the mat. Pad the knee with a blanket if needed. Keep the front knee over the ankle, not far past the toes. Let the hips sink forward and down until you feel a stretch in the front of the back hip. Lift the chest so the torso rises over the hips, and reach the arms up alongside the ears. Breathe in to lengthen. Breathe out and sink a little deeper.
lsit: L-Sit. Hands beside the hips, straighten the arms and press the hips off the floor. Lift the straight legs level with the floor. Keep breathing. To make it easier, bend the knees.
lungetwist: Low Lunge Twist. From a lunge, place the bottom hand on the floor inside the front foot. Keep the back leg long. Twist toward the front leg and reach the top arm straight up, stacking it over the bottom arm. Breathe in to lengthen, breathe out to turn. Lower the back knee if needed.
marichi1: Marichi One. Sit with both legs long. Bend one knee, foot flat, heel near the sitting bone. Keep the extended leg straight and the foot flexed. Wrap the arm on the bent knee side around the shin and clasp the hands behind the back. Lengthen the spine, then fold forward over the straight leg, leading with the chest. Breathe in to lengthen, out to fold. If the hands do not meet, hold a strap.
marichi3: Marichi Three. Sit with both legs long. Bend one knee and place the foot flat near the sitting bone, knee pointing up. Keep the extended leg straight. Sit tall before you twist, then turn the chest toward the bent knee. Hook the opposite elbow outside the knee and place the other hand behind you. Breathe in to grow taller, breathe out to turn a little more. If the back rounds, sit on a folded blanket.
mountain: Mountain. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms resting by your sides. Point the toes straight ahead so the feet are parallel, and spread your weight evenly between both feet. Straighten the legs without locking the knees. Stack the shoulders over the hips, and keep both shoulders and both hips level. Let the arms hang alongside the body, fingertips pointing down. Breathe in slowly through the nose, and breathe out just as slowly.
onelegbridge: One-Legged Bridge. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Lift the hips, then extend one leg toward the ceiling. Keep the hips high and level. Stack the grounded knee over its ankle. Breathe steadily. Lower the hips a little to make it easier.
onelegwheel: One-Legged Wheel. From wheel, shift your weight onto one foot and extend the other leg toward the ceiling. Press the floor away through straight arms. Keep the hips high as the leg rises. Breathe steadily.
peacock: Peacock. Kneel with the hands down, fingers pointing back, elbows tucked into the belly. Straighten the legs and squeeze them together. Lean forward until the body is level. Breathe. Keep the toes down to start.
pigeon: Pigeon. From downward dog, bring one knee forward behind your wrist and let that shin rest across the mat. Extend the back leg straight behind you, top of the foot down. Square your hips to the front of the mat. If the front hip lifts off the floor, slide a block or blanket under it for support. Walk your hands back toward your hips and lift your chest. Keep the spine long and the shoulders soft. Breathe into the front hip and stay steady.
plank: Plank. From hands and knees, step back onto the balls of the feet. Stack the shoulders over the wrists, fingers pointing to the top of the mat. Straighten the arms and push the floor away. Press back through the heels and make one line from the shoulders to the heels, with the hips neither high nor sagging. Breathe steadily. Lower the knees if you need to.
plow: Plow. From your back, press your hands into the mat and roll your legs up and over your head with control. Lift your hips until they stack over your shoulders. Keep your legs straight and lower your toes toward the floor behind you. If the toes do not reach, rest your feet on a block or bend your knees. Keep your head still and your gaze up, with no turning of the neck. Breathe slowly into your back body.
prayerwrists: Prayer Wrist Stretch. Sit tall and press your palms together in front of your chest, fingers pointing up, elbows wide. Keeping the heels of the hands pressed together, slowly lower the hands toward your belly until you feel the stretch in the wrists. Shoulders soft. Breathe in, and breathe out slowly.
puppy: Puppy. Start on your hands and knees. Keep your hips stacked over your knees and walk your hands forward. Straighten your arms and reach through your fingertips. Let your chest lower toward the floor and rest your forehead on the mat or on a block. Keep a small lift in the belly so the lower back does not sink. If your shoulders feel strained, bring your hands a little wider. Breathe into your upper back. With each exhale, let the chest sink a little lower.
pyramid: Pyramid. Step one foot back, turn the back toes out slightly, and square the hips to the front. Keep both legs straight, with a small bend in the front knee. Breathing in, lengthen the spine. Breathing out, hinge forward over the front leg from the hips, keeping the back long. Breathe evenly. If the hamstrings are tight, bend the front knee more rather than rounding the back.
quadlunge: Low Lunge Quad Stretch. From a lunge, lower the back knee to the mat, padded if you need it. Stack the front knee over the ankle. Bend the back knee and reach back to hold the foot. Draw the heel toward the hip. Lift the chest and tuck the tailbone to feel the stretch in the front of the thigh. Breathe slowly. If you cannot reach the foot, use a strap or keep the back toes down.
rabbit: Rabbit. Sit on your heels and hold your heels with your hands. Tuck your chin and round forward, placing the crown of your head lightly near your knees. Lift your hips over your knees. Keep the weight light on your head, with most of it in your shins. Breathe into your upper back.
ragdoll: Ragdoll. From standing, fold forward from the hips. Bend the knees generously so the belly rests on the thighs. Hold opposite elbows and let the arms hang. Let the torso hang heavy, with the head and neck loose. Shift your weight slightly toward the balls of the feet. Sway gently if you like. Breathe slowly, letting each exhale release the back a little more. To come up, keep the knees bent and roll up slowly.
reclinedbigtoe: Reclined Hand to Big Toe. Lie on your back with both legs long. Hug one knee in, then hold the big toe or loop a strap around the foot. Straighten the lifted leg and bring it toward vertical. Keep the bottom leg long on the mat with the foot flexed. If the lifted leg will not straighten, use the strap and lower the leg a little. Keep both hips level and your shoulders and head resting down. Breathe slowly into the back of the lifted leg.
reclinedbigtoeside: Reclined Big Toe to the Side. Lie on your back with both legs long. Draw one knee in and hold the big toe, or loop a strap around the foot. Straighten the leg toward the ceiling, then open it out to the side. Keep the bottom leg long and the foot flexed. Keep both shoulders on the mat as the leg opens. Press the opposite hip down so the pelvis stays steady. Breathe slowly. If the leg will not straighten, use a strap or rest the leg on a block.
reclinedbound: Reclined Bound Angle. Lie on your back. Bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees open out to the sides. Let your knees release toward the floor. If they feel strained, support each one with a block or cushion. Rest your whole back on the mat, head and shoulders heavy. Let your arms rest by your sides, palms up, or place one hand on your belly. Breathe slowly and deeply. Let your belly rise as you breathe in and fall as you breathe out.
reclinedpigeon: Reclined Figure Four. Lie on your back with both knees bent and feet on the floor. Cross one ankle over the opposite thigh, just above the knee, and flex that foot. Lift the bottom foot and reach your hands behind the bottom thigh. Draw the thigh in toward your chest. Keep your head and shoulders resting on the mat. If you cannot reach, keep the bottom foot on the floor or use a strap. Breathe into the outer hip of the crossed leg.
reverseprayer: Reverse Prayer Hands. Sit tall. Turn the backs of your hands together, fingers pointing down, in front of your belly. Lift the elbows out to the sides and slowly draw the hands up toward your chest, keeping the backs of the hands touching. Go gently; this one can be strong. Keep breathing.
reversetable: Reverse Tabletop. Sit with the knees bent, feet flat, and hands behind the hips, fingers forward. Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the torso is parallel to the floor. Keep the arms straight with the wrists under the shoulders. Stack the knees over the ankles. Breathe steadily.
reversewarrior: Reverse Warrior. From Warrior Two, turn the front palm up and reach the front arm up and back. Let the back hand rest lightly on the back leg. Keep the front knee bent over the ankle, toes pointing straight down the mat. Keep the back leg straight and strong. Lean back from the ribs, lengthening both sides of the waist rather than collapsing. Breathe into the long side of the body.
revhalfmoon: Revolved Half Moon. From Standing Split, place the bottom hand on a block under the shoulder. Straighten the standing leg and lift the back leg to hip height. Twist the chest open and stack the top arm over the bottom arm. Keep the hips level as you twist. Breathe steadily. Use a block to bring the floor closer.
revheadtoknee: Revolved Head to Knee. Sit with the legs wide, then bend one knee and bring that foot to the inner thigh. Keep the extended leg straight and reach through the heel. Lean sideways over the straight leg, lower arm resting inside it. Turn the chest up toward the ceiling. Reach the top arm overhead toward the foot. Keep both sitting bones grounded. Breathe in to lengthen the side, breathe out to turn. If the hamstring pulls, bend the knee slightly.
revsideangle: Revolved Side Angle. From a high lunge, bring the palms together at the chest. Twist and hook the elbow to the outside of the front knee. Straighten the back leg and press through the back heel, making one line from the heel through the crown. Breathe in to lengthen, breathe out to turn. To make it easier, lower the back knee.
revtriangle: Revolved Triangle. Step one foot back, hips facing the front, and keep both legs straight. Hinge forward over the front leg with a long spine first. Then place the bottom hand on a block, twist, and reach the top arm straight up. Stack the top arm over the bottom arm. Breathe in to lengthen, breathe out to turn. A block under the bottom hand makes this easier.
runnerslunge: Runner's Lunge. From a forward fold, step one foot back into a lunge. Frame the front foot with the hands, under the shoulders. Stack the front knee over the ankle. Straighten the back leg and press through the back heel. Lengthen from the heel to the crown. Breathe steadily. You can lower the back knee to rest.
saddle: Saddle. Sit between the heels with the knees close together. Lean back slowly onto the hands, then the forearms. Lower the back toward the mat, or rest it on a bolster. Keep the knees close. If they lift, add more padding under the back. Rest the arms by your sides or overhead. Breathe slowly into the front of the thighs. If you feel any pain in the knees or lower back, come up and use more support. To come out, press into the forearms and sit up slowly.
savasana: Resting Pose. Lie on your back with the legs long and the feet falling open. Rest the arms a little away from the body, palms up. Close the eyes. Let the back of the head, the shoulders, and the hips grow heavy on the mat. Soften the jaw and the space between the eyebrows. Let the breath move on its own. If the lower back feels tight, bend the knees or place a cushion under them. Stay here and rest. There is nothing to do.
scorpion: Scorpion. From forearm stand, press the forearms flat, shoulders over elbows. Keep the hips stacked, then bend the knees and let the feet drift toward the head. Breathe. Use a wall while learning.
seatedfold: Seated Forward Fold. Sit with the legs extended in front of you and flex the feet, toes pointing up. Breathe in and lengthen the spine. Breathe out and fold forward from the hips, leading with the chest. Hold the shins, ankles or feet, wherever you reach with a long back. Bend the knees as much as you need to keep the fold coming from the hips rather than the lower back. A blanket under the seat helps. Breathe slowly, and let each exhale deepen the fold a little, without pulling.
seatedtwist: Half Lord of the Fishes. Sit tall, bend one knee, and step that foot over the other leg, sole flat on the floor. Keep the top knee pointing up. Place your back hand on the floor behind you for support. Lengthen your spine first, then twist from the waist without leaning back. Hug the knee with your front arm. Inhale to grow taller, exhale to turn a little more.
shoulderstand: Shoulder Stand. Lie on your back with a folded blanket under the shoulders and the head on the floor. Lift the legs and hips and support the back with the hands. Walk the hands toward the shoulder blades to lift the hips over the shoulders. Reach the feet straight up and keep both legs straight. Keep the head still and do not turn it while you are up. Press the upper arms down and breathe slowly. For an easier version, rest the legs up a wall.
sideangle: Extended Side Angle. Step the feet wide and bend the front knee over the ankle, thigh toward parallel. Rest the bottom forearm on the front thigh, or the hand on a block. Keep the back leg straight and press into the outer edge of the back foot. Extend the top arm over the ear, making one long line from the back heel to the fingertips. Breathe into the top ribs.
sidebend: Standing Side Bend. Stand tall and reach both arms overhead, alongside your ears. Keep both legs straight and grounded. Reach over to one side. Keep your hips level and both sides of the waist long. Breathe into the open side.
sidecrow: Side Crow. Squat with the knees together and twist, placing both hands on the floor. Bend the elbows to make a shelf, and stack the knees on the outer arm. Shift forward, lifting the hips higher than the shoulders. Breathe. Keep the toes down to practice.
sideplank: Side Plank. From plank, roll onto the outer edge of one foot and stack the feet, or stagger them for balance. Keep the supporting arm straight, shoulder over wrist. Lift the bottom hip into one line from shoulders to feet. Reach the top arm straight up. Breathe steadily. Lower the bottom knee for an easier version.
sideplankstar: Side Plank Star. From side plank, lift the top leg and reach the top arm straight up. Press the floor away through the supporting arm. Lift the hips into one line from head to heel. Breathe steadily. To make it easier, rest the bottom knee down.
sideplanktree: Side Plank Tree. From side plank, place the top foot on the inner thigh of the bottom leg. Keep the supporting arm straight. Lift the hips so the body stays in one line. Breathe slowly. To make it easier, lower the bottom knee.
skandasana: Side Lunge. Start in a wide stance with the toes turned slightly out. Bend one knee and sink the hips low toward that heel. Straighten the other leg, toes pointing up. Keep the bent heel down if you can. Lift the chest, hands at the heart or on the floor in front of you. Breathe steadily into the inner thigh. If the heel lifts, place a rolled mat under it.
sleepingpigeon: Sleeping Pigeon. From pigeon, with your front shin across the mat and back leg extended straight behind you, walk your hands forward. Keep the hips level as you fold. Lower your chest toward the floor and rest your forehead on your hands or forearms. If the front hip lifts, support it with a block or blanket. Keep the back leg long, top of the foot down. Let your shoulders relax. Breathe slowly into the outer hip, and let each exhale release some effort.
sphinx: Sphinx. Lie on your belly and set the elbows directly under the shoulders, forearms parallel on the mat. Press the forearms down and lift the chest forward and up. Let the pelvis stay heavy on the floor. Lengthen the legs along the mat, tops of the feet down. Draw the shoulders away from the ears. Breathe slowly into the chest. If the low back feels tight, slide the elbows forward.
splits: Monkey Pose. Begin in Half Splits with blocks on either side of the front leg. Slowly slide the front heel forward and the back knee back, lowering the hips toward the floor. Keep the front leg straight, kneecap up, and the back leg straight behind you. Keep the hips facing the front. Place a block under the front hip and stop wherever you feel a strong stretch. Sit tall over the hips and lift through the chest. Breathe slowly and stay steady. Do not force the depth.
staff: Staff. Sit with the legs extended straight in front of you. Flex the feet so the toes point up, and press the backs of the thighs down. Place the palms beside the hips, under the shoulders. Sit tall, stacking the shoulders over the hips rather than leaning back. If the lower back rounds, sit on a folded blanket or a block, or bend the knees slightly. Breathe in and sit taller.
standingbackbend: Standing Backbend. Keep the legs strong. Reach the arms up, then lift the chest and lean back gently, arms in line with the torso. Keep the lower back long. Breathe in as you lift.
standingsplit: Standing Split. From a forward fold, shift your weight onto the standing foot and lift the other leg up behind you. Fold the torso down along the standing leg, hands on the floor or on blocks. Keep both legs straight. Lift the back leg higher while the hips stay square. Breathe out and let the head hang.
star: Five-Pointed Star. Step the feet wide apart, toes pointing forward. Keep both legs straight. Lift the arms out wide, a little above shoulder height. Stand tall through the crown and reach out through the hands and feet. Breathe in and out, slow and steady.
sugarcane: Sugarcane. From half moon, keep the standing leg straight and the bottom hand on the floor or a block. Bend the top knee and reach back to hold the ankle or foot. Stack the top shoulder over the bottom one. Breathe steadily.
superman: Superman. Lie on your belly with the arms forward. Breathe in and lift the chest, arms, and legs. Lift with the back muscles, not the neck, gaze down. Reach the arms long. Keep both knees straight as the legs lift. Keep breathing.
supinelegsup: Supine Leg Raise. Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, palms down. Lift your legs up toward vertical and straighten them. Press your lower back into the mat. If your lower back lifts, bend your knees slightly. Keep your neck and shoulders relaxed. Breathe steadily.
supinetwist: Supine Twist. Lie on your back and hug your knees in. Open your arms out to the sides at shoulder height. Stack your knees and let them drop together toward the floor on one side. Keep both shoulders resting on the mat. If the top shoulder lifts, place a block or cushion under your knees. Turn your gaze away from your knees if your neck is comfortable. Let your arms be heavy. Breathe into your side ribs and let each exhale soften the twist.
supportedbridge: Supported Bridge. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart. Press into your feet, lift your hips, and slide a block under your sacrum, the flat bone at the base of your spine. Lower your weight onto the block and let your hips be fully supported. Stack your knees over your ankles. Rest your arms by your sides, palms up. Let your head be heavy. To come out, lift your hips and remove the block. Breathe slowly and stay still.
tabletop: Tabletop. Come onto hands and knees. Stack the wrists under the shoulders and the knees under the hips. Level the spine from the hips to the shoulders, with the neck long and the gaze down. Breathe in and out slowly here.
tabletoplegs: Supine Tabletop. Lie on your back with the arms by your sides. Lift one leg, then the other, into tabletop. Stack the knees directly over the hips. Bring the shins parallel to the floor. Press the lower back gently into the mat. Draw the ribs down and keep the neck relaxed. Breathe out fully to firm the belly. If the lower back lifts, lower one foot to the floor.
tabletwist: Seated Spinal Twist. Sit with one leg extended and the foot flexed. Bend the other knee and place that foot flat near the opposite thigh. Keep the extended leg straight. Place your back hand on the floor behind you. Sit tall, then twist from the waist toward the bent knee. Hug the knee with your front arm, or hook the elbow outside it. Inhale to lengthen, and exhale to turn a little more.
threadneedle: Thread the Needle. Start on your hands and knees, hips over knees. Slide one arm under your body, palm up, until that shoulder and ear rest on the mat. Keep your hips stacked over your knees as you settle. Extend the top arm forward on the mat, or wrap it behind your back. Let your neck relax and your forehead stay soft. Breathe into the back of the shoulder, and soften a little more with each exhale.
threeleggeddog: Three-Legged Dog. From downward dog, lift one leg in line with your spine. Keep it straight and reach through the heel. Keep the hips level. Press the floor away through straight arms. Breathe.
thunderbolt: Thunderbolt. Kneel with your knees together and the tops of your feet on the mat. Sit back onto your heels. If your ankles or knees feel strained, place a folded blanket under your shins or a cushion between your hips and heels. Stack your shoulders over your hips and sit tall, crown of the head reaching up. Rest your hands on your thighs. Relax your shoulders and your face. Breathe slowly and evenly through the nose, and let the belly soften on each exhale. Stay steady here.
tiger: Tiger. From hands and knees, keep the wrists under the shoulders. Lift one knee and draw the foot toward the head. Lift the gaze and open the chest. Breathe steadily and keep the hips level.
toestand: Toe Stand. From a squat, lift your heels and balance on the balls of your feet. Sink your hips down toward your heels. Lengthen your spine and lift your chest. Bring your hands together at your heart. Breathe slowly.
tolasana: Scale. Sit cross-legged or in lotus, hands beside the hips. Press down through straight arms and lift the hips clear of the mat. Lift the chest. Breathe. Blocks under the hands help.
tortoise: Tortoise. Sit with the legs wide and the knees bent. Fold forward and slide the arms under the knees, reaching them out to the sides, palms down. Straighten the legs as the arms slide further under. Fold the chest down toward the floor. Keep the back of the neck long. Breathe slowly into the back. This is a deep pose, so keep the knees bent if the lower back strains.
tree: Tree. Stand tall with the standing toes pointing forward. Shift your weight into one foot and place the lifted foot on the inner calf or inner thigh, never on the knee. Open the lifted knee out to the side. Keep the standing leg firm and the standing hip stacked over the ankle. Keep the hips level and grow tall. Press the palms together at the heart or overhead. Breathe slowly, gaze on one still point.
triangle: Triangle. Step the feet wide, front toes down the mat, heels in one line. Keep both legs long, with only a micro-bend in the front knee. Reach out over the front leg, then tip down and rest the bottom hand on the shin or a block. Keep both sides of the waist long. Stack the top arm over the bottom arm and reach up through the fingertips. Breathe into the ribs.
tripodheadstand: Tripod Headstand. Place the crown of the head and both hands on the mat in a triangle, elbows bent to ninety degrees, forearms vertical. Walk the feet in and lift the hips over the shoulders. Lift the legs slowly and reach the feet straight up over the hips. Press firmly through the hands. Breathe. Practice at a wall.
updog: Upward Dog. From low to the mat, press the tops of the feet down and straighten the arms, shoulders over wrists. Lift the chest and the thighs off the mat, legs straight. Draw the shoulders away from the ears. Breathe in as you rise.
upsalute: Upward Salute. Stand with the feet parallel and the legs straight. Breathe in and sweep the arms up alongside the ears, fingertips reaching toward the ceiling. Keep the shoulders over the hips and lift from the ribs, not the lower back. Breathe steadily.
upwardplank: Upward Plank. Sit with the legs long and the hands behind the hips, fingers toward the feet. Press the floor away and lift the hips into one line from shoulders to feet. Keep the arms straight and the legs straight, pressing the soles toward the mat. Breathe steadily. Bend the knees for an easier version.
warrior1: Warrior One. From standing, step one foot back a long stride and turn the back foot out slightly. Bend the front knee toward ninety degrees, knee stacked over the ankle. Keep the back leg straight and press the back heel into the mat. Lift the torso upright over the pelvis and reach both arms up alongside the ears, elbows straight, fingertips reaching up. Breathe steadily and stay tall.
warrior2: Warrior Two. Step the feet wide. Point the front toes straight down the mat, and turn the back toes in, almost parallel to the back edge. Line up the front heel with the back heel. Bend the front knee over the ankle, tracking toward the second toe. Keep the back leg straight and the torso upright over the pelvis. Reach the arms out at shoulder height, palms down, wrists long. Breathe evenly, gazing past the front hand.
warrior3: Warrior Three. From standing, shift your weight into one leg. Tip the torso forward as the back leg lifts, until both reach hip height. Keep the standing leg straight with a micro-bend, hip stacked over the ankle. Flex the lifted foot so the toes point down. Reach from the lifted heel to the crown in one long line. Breathe steadily. Blocks help.
warrior3hands: Airplane. Stand on one leg and hinge forward from the hips, lifting the back leg behind you. Bring the torso parallel to the floor and lift the back leg to hip height. Keep the standing leg straight. Sweep the arms back alongside the body, palms down. Keep the hips level and the neck long. Breathe steadily. Bend the standing knee slightly if balance is hard.
wheel: Wheel. Lie on your back, feet parallel near the hips, hands by the ears. Press into the hands and feet and lift. Straighten the arms and move the chest toward the wall behind you, shoulders over wrists. Breathe steadily. Bridge is a fine alternative.
widechild: Extended Child. Kneel with the big toes touching and the knees apart. Sit the hips back toward the heels. Walk the hands forward and lengthen the arms. Lower the chest and forehead toward the mat. Let the shoulders soften and the neck relax. If the hips do not reach the heels, place a cushion between them. If the forehead does not reach the floor, rest it on a block. Breathe slowly into the back of the ribs. Let the spine lengthen a little with each breath out. Stay here.
widefold: Wide-Legged Forward Fold. Step the feet wide apart and turn the toes straight ahead so the outer edges of the feet are parallel. Hands on the hips, lengthen the spine and fold forward from the hips. Bring the hands to the mat, directly under the shoulders. Keep the legs straight and lift the kneecaps, with weight even in both feet so the hips stay level. If the floor feels far away, bend the knees a little or put the hands on blocks. Breathe slowly and steadily.
widefoldtwist: Revolved Wide-Legged Fold. Step the feet wide and fold forward with a long spine. Plant one hand under your face and reach the other arm up. Keep both legs straight. Press the bottom hand down through a straight arm. Keep the hips level as the chest turns. Breathe in to lengthen, out to turn.
wideseated: Wide Angle Seated Fold. Sit tall and open your legs wide apart. Keep both legs straight with your kneecaps facing up, and flex your feet. Place your hands on the floor in front of you. Inhale to lengthen your spine. Exhale and walk your hands forward, folding from the hips. If your back rounds, sit on a folded blanket and bend the knees slightly. Stop where you can still keep the spine long. Breathe steadily and let the inner legs lengthen.
wideseatedside: Wide Seated Side Bend. Sit with the legs wide apart. Keep both legs straight, kneecaps to the ceiling. Lean sideways over one leg, resting the lower hand on the shin or the floor. Turn the chest toward the ceiling. Reach the top arm overhead toward the foot. Keep both sitting bones on the mat. Breathe in to lengthen the side body, breathe out to lean a little further. Sit on a folded blanket if the back rounds.
wildthing: Wild Thing. From Side Plank, step the top foot behind you and plant the sole on the mat with the knee bent. Keep the supporting arm straight. Press the hips up and let the chest arch open. Reach the free arm overhead toward the floor. Breathe.
windrelieving: Wind Relieving Pose. Lie on your back with both legs long. Bend one knee and hug it in toward your chest with both hands. Keep the other leg long on the mat, the foot flexed and the back of the leg reaching down. Keep your head and shoulders resting on the mat. Relax your shoulders away from your ears. If holding the shin strains your knee, hold the back of the thigh instead. Breathe into your belly against the thigh, and let each exhale draw the knee a little closer.
wristext: Wrist Extension. Reach one arm forward at shoulder height, palm facing away, fingers pointing up. With the other hand, gently draw the fingers back toward you until you feel a stretch along the inside of the forearm. Keep the elbow long and the shoulders relaxed. Breathe slowly.
wristflex: Wrist Flexion. Reach one arm forward at shoulder height and let the fingers point down, the back of the hand facing forward. With the other hand, gently press the back of the hand toward you until you feel a stretch along the top of the forearm. Shoulders down, breath slow.
wristrelease: Wrist Release. Come onto your hands and knees. Lift one hand at a time and turn it so the fingers point back toward your knees, palms flat on the mat. Keep the arms long, and very slowly lean your hips back until you feel a gentle stretch along the inner forearms. Only a little weight in the hands. Breathe slowly, and ease off if anything feels sharp.
